presentation.label: 8-bit sampler
presentation.summary: Plays a Flex sample like an 8-bit tracker: gritty, held samples and a cyclic stretch that pulls pitch and time apart, on whole samples or slices.
presentation.overview: Amiga is a track machine modelled on how a home computer's 8-bit sound chip and its tracker software played samples. It plays the track's Flex sample through the stock reader, reduces its word length and storage rate before the Octatrack repitches it, and can restart the sample every few milliseconds a little further on, so PTCH changes the pitch and SPD the length. Each restart crossfades out of the sample itself over half a cycle, as Amigo's grains do, and a sliced note stretches inside its slice. RATE is stock's own, forwards and backwards. The track's filter, AMP, LFOs and effects follow as for any sample.
highlights: SPD sets how fast the note moves through the sample and GRN the cycle, 96 to 4128 samples: half speed, about twice as fast or a held sound, at any pitch.
Slices stretch too: SLIC on, STRT picks the slice, and the stretch stays inside it.
Every restart crossfades over half a cycle, whichever way the note is going.
STR can turn the stretch into a pitch shift of up to an octave either way.
RATE is stock's own: forwards, backwards and slower, with the stretch following it both ways.
SRR lowers the storage rate, BITS sets the word from 4 to 16 bits (8 by default), LED adds a fixed lowpass.
RATE, SPD and GRN take parameter locks, LFOs and scenes, as SRC knobs do.
usage: Double-tap a track key (or open SRC SETUP), move to AMIGA in the machine list and press YES.
Double-tap the track key again and pick a sample from the Flex list, as for a Flex track.
Open SRC: knob D is RATE, E is SPD, F is GRN.

controls.name: RATE
controls.doc: Stock's RATE, -64 to +63: speed and pitch together, backwards below 0. The stretch follows it both ways. SRC knob D.

controls.name: SPD
controls.doc: How fast the note moves through the sample, whatever the pitch: 64 is its own speed, 32 half, 0 holds. SRC knob E.

controls.name: GRN
controls.doc: The stretch's cycle, 96 to 4128 samples; 1120 by default. Each restart crossfades over half of it. SRC knob F.

controls.name: LED
controls.doc: A fixed two-pole lowpass on the stored sample. SRC SETUP knob C.

controls.name: SRR
controls.doc: Storage rate: 16/(16+SRR) of the sample's own, each stored sample an average, then held. SRC SETUP knob D.

controls.name: STR
controls.doc: The stretch: OFF plays as FLEX, ON stretches, PCH shifts the pitch by SPD at the note's own length. SRC SETUP knob E.

controls.name: BITS
controls.doc: Word length from 4 to 16 bits; the saved value is bits minus 4. 16 leaves the sample's own word. SRC SETUP knob F.

limitations: USB only: it loads on the Modwerk base over USB (it needs the base's machine list and START dispatch) and has no card build.
Experimental: played and measured on one MKII on a development base; TESTING.md lists what was not tried.

Measured on 0.1.0-experimental, an MKII: one Amiga track beside seven FLEX tracks added 5.5 points to the frame interrupt at the defaults and up to 13.8 with PTCH +12, SRR and LED; eight Amiga tracks reached the base's frame guard, which skipped 17 % of their renders (dropouts). This version has not been measured on a unit; count on a few Amiga tracks, not eight. Other installed modules leave less room: beside fifteen of them and three sounding FLEX tracks, one Amiga track took 12.6 to 16 points.
With a USB recording running as well, one Amiga track (0.1.0-experimental) at PTCH +12 with SRR and LED on beside seven FLEX tracks froze the unit until a power cycle.
No stock RTRG or RTIM on an Amiga track: SPD and GRN take their knobs.
Stock's own time-stretch (TSTR) is off on an Amiga track, and SETUP's LEN switch is LED: the track always uses stock's default length setting, LEN OFF.
SRR, LED, STR and BITS are SETUP values: one for the Part, without locks or LFOs.
A sliced note is stretched when it is one slice, as stock plays it with SETUP's LEN off; SRR, BITS and LED work either way.
The cycle length is in samples, not tied to the tempo.
The crossfade reads the sample itself. A recorder buffer that is recording, or a sample the module cannot read, restarts with a short fade-out of the step instead.
A stretched note that is not looped ends when SPD has carried it to the end of the sample, even if LEN would stop a FLEX note sooner by time.
A project opened without the module plays Amiga tracks as FLEX and reads SPD and GRN as stock's RTRG and RTIM, and LED, SRR, STR and BITS as SETUP's LEN, RATE, TSTR and TSNS.
Leaving Amiga for another machine puts the track's SRC settings back to FLEX defaults.
Before a trial of the module ends or the module is removed, put its tracks on another machine: the base refuses to take a machine away from a track that names it.

storage.label: Module image and memory
storage.conditions: The USB package of this source (SHA-256 6bb8e598b76e359bda78fb420abaa96926ff8e8f3265b78932ef4599755c9b67, built by npm run module:dev -- amiga --build-only): 11,792 bytes of code and data and 2,092 of bss, the eight voices' state and the sample descriptions for the crossfade. The loader's own record for the module and the stack the render uses are not counted. The loader allows a module 128 KiB.

processing.label: ColdFire, in the frame interrupt
processing.display: Not measured in cycles; 0.1.0 measured 5.5 to 13.8 points of a frame a track
processing.conditions: No worst case in cycles exists, and this version has not been measured on a unit. On the owner's MKII with 0.1.0-experimental (development twin d8fae687 of the base, 11 November 2026; five seconds of a 131 BPM pattern, eight tracks playing loops, one reading each) the frame interrupt read 63.7 % with eight FLEX tracks, 69.2 % with track 1 on Amiga at the defaults and 77.5 % with PTCH +12, SRR and LED; eight Amiga tracks at the defaults read 79.2 % with 16.9 % of their renders skipped by the base's frame guard. These are means over five seconds, not a longest frame. For this version ot_emu counts 124 to 4,762 instructions of the engine's own code per audio frame of one track (worst frame 6,488), where 0.1.0 counted 300 to 5,355 (worst 6,501); the unit's time did not follow such counts.

impact.conditions: CPU from frame-interrupt readings of 0.1.0-experimental on an MKII (one Amiga track playing a loop beside seven FLEX tracks, from the defaults to PTCH +12 with SRR and LED on, and eight Amiga tracks at the defaults; means, one reading each); this version not yet measured on a unit. Memory from this package's sizes, all eight voices included whether used or not.

cpu.rationale: The ColdFire reworks the track's source frames in the frame interrupt: the word and rate reduction, the lowpass and the cyclic restarts with their crossfades, which read the sample itself. With 0.1.0 one Amiga track added 5.5 points of the frame at the defaults and 13.8 with PTCH +12, SRR and LED against a FLEX track on the same unit; eight at the defaults reached the base's 80 % frame guard, which skipped 16.9 % of their renders. This version no longer copies every frame into a memory, which the emulator counts as cheaper; it has not been measured on a unit. Worst-case cycles are not measured.

dsp.rationale: No DSP program, effect slot or DSP state is added. The reworked frames go to the DSP through the stock FLEX path, which repitches and filters them as it does a FLEX track's.

memory.rationale: 11,792 bytes of code and data and 2,092 of bss in the package, about 14 KiB of the 128 KiB the loader allows a module. No sample RAM is taken and no stock buffer is reused: the crossfade reads the track's own sample where stock keeps it.

tests.summary: Host gate on the engine (verify.py, 72 checks: the crunch, the stretch's timing and its crossfades out of the sample, pages, words and directions), a comparison of the crossfades with Amigo's (reference/amigo_check.py, the owner's installed plug-in), an emulator count of its instructions (bench.py), and RAM trials of 0.1.0-experimental on the owner's MKII on a development base, 11 November 2026. This version has not run on a unit yet. TESTING.md lists what was not tried.
gates: python3 -B reference/amigo_check.py <a folder with the Amigo host and its default state> (macOS with Amigo installed)
python3 -B bench.py --emulator <ot_emu> --main <a MAIN image the emulator boots> --output <new private folder>

tutorial.title: Quick tutorial
steps: Put a drum loop on an Amiga track and play it. At the defaults it is the loop at 8 bits.
Turn PTCH up a few semitones: the loop keeps its length and starts to flutter. Turn GRN for the size of the flutter.
Turn SPD down to 32 for half speed at the same pitch, or all the way to 0 to hold the sound where it is.
Turn RATE below 0: the loop runs backwards, still stretched.
On SRC SETUP, turn SRR up to about 20 for a grainy, folded top end, and switch LED on to take the edge off it.
Put a sliced loop on the track, switch SLIC on in SRC SETUP and trig slices with STRT locks: turn PTCH and each slice keeps its length, SPD and GRN stretch inside it.

access.location: The track's machine list (double-tap TRACK, or SRC SETUP)
steps: Double-tap a track key, choose AMIGA in the machine list and press YES, then double-tap again and pick a Flex sample.
On SRC, turn PTCH: the pitch moves and the length stays. Turn SPD (knob E) for the length and GRN (knob F) for the flutter; RATE (knob D) is stock's, backwards below 0.
On SRC SETUP, raise SRR for a lower sample rate. LED, STR and BITS are beside it.
